title: Circumcision and Divine Discipline
english: It is not short-lived nor temporary; rather, they will rejoice forever, because God dwells in them. For how could they not always rejoice when God is present, tabernacling as if in his own temple? For how could those who have God in themselves, dwelling and walking about, be near to joy, when the distance from God, caused by sin capturing them, is near to wails and lamentations?

The preceding words shall be said concerning the arrival of the Savior, the joy of all those waiting for his human appearance (Ps 5:12ab); for the prophets and those who understand the prophecies hoped for this. For the Word of God arrived having become flesh to dwell in those believing in him; for he says, 'The Word became flesh and dwelt among us' (John 1:14). Thus, having dwelt, those who received him in themselves will rejoice forever; for they see the glory of the Word having tabernacled among them through the flesh, as the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth; those of this time, rejoicing forever, having seen by work the glory of the one as the only-begotten from the Father, say: 'Even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, but now we no longer know him, having the vision of his glory as the only-begotten from the Father' (2 Cor 5:16).
The cross is both a weapon and a crown; a weapon for those warring, a crown for those conquering. And again: a weapon for the soldiers, a crown for those reigning.

But he is contained in hymns having a more divine thought, and he himself is such; and he also sees toward the end the most perfect things regarding the eighth. It must be considered what the spiritual circumcision is, which one having God is circumcised, not necessarily one being circumcised according to the flesh. For the prophet says to those striving only according to the flesh: 'Be circumcised to your God, and do not circumcise the flesh of your uncircumcision' (Rom 2:29); and the same prophet says: 'All Gentiles are uncircumcised in the flesh, but the house of Israel are uncircumcised in their hearts' (Jeremiah 9:26). Therefore, he who is sensibly circumcised removes something of that which serves the generation of the member, just as he who casting out every thought friendly to the generation of the intellect circumcises the heart. This circumcision they have, the truly [believing]...

Those devoted to the things of the Lord, so as to please Him. For circumcision is established on the eighth day; for the circumcised must overcome the world that was created in six days, and this is to become on the seventh day a true, holy, and sweet Sabbath. And since the ceasing from worldly things is not sufficient for perfect blessedness, it is necessary to receive, after the Sabbath, a super-cosmic state as the eighth. He who has been tempted by this desire will not love the world nor the things in it. Toward this spiritual understanding he leads us, and the mixture with the command of the sensible circumcision does not save the Logos if it remains merely in bare histories: 'Every male shall be circumcised on the eighth day' (Exodus 12:48), he says. Regarding the transgression of what was commanded, a threat of destruction is set against the child not circumcised on the eighth day, but not against the parents or the one raising the child otherwise; for the threat seemed to be reasonable, if it were brought upon one of these, not saving the follower of the eight-day child from doing it, and especially the intention to keep the commandment of God.

He is reproved in anger, and his sins are not made manifest (Ps 6:2); being led by Him according to a bitter and painful guidance, just as one who has fallen under the wraths of God, receiving the sensation of the cause of the evil having happened, is being disciplined in anger for suffering these things. By this thought is said, regarding the wrath led toward the senses: 'I will endure the wrath of the Lord until I do wrong to Him,' so as not to justify my judgment and to turn away my judgment and to drive me into the light. For if one, having been led into such a state, knows that the wrath has been brought upon him from God by a way of healing, he will not at all be unwilling to be subject to it, so that the judgment might be justified on account of Him who judges not thus. For not he who, having endured the wrath according to the purpose of the one who led him, will be driven into the light by God, having turned away the judgment from Him. If, therefore, of those being reproved and being disciplined, some are so through anger and wrath, and others through logical teaching, these things are to be completed, and through toil they come to reproof and discipline. title: The Return of the Soul and the New Man
english: the voluntary application of rebuke and instruction through the word

The same. When such a vision is presented: since my soul, sinning, had turned away toward its own evil, having turned back to itself, calling itself back according to [the Psalm], 'Turn back, you sons who have gone away' (Ps 6:7), to ransom itself from the sins that have grown distant and from the evil powers working them.

Those who imply that the upcoming words refer to common death err, but rather they act impiously. For the holy men do not have remembrance of God and the common life only then, but much more so, as they are separated from the corruptible body.

What do you say? Since no one, having remembered you, becomes in death—for sin does not die (and he is not the one separating the sinning soul from a virtuous life)—but I desire to have remembrance of you; for this purpose, having poured out your goodness: save me, so that I may not be overcome by the weakness and trouble that is present against me, and be crushed by death. For it is not said, 'He does not remember God in death' (Ps 6:5), but rather, 'He who remembers him is not in death,' as the Savior says, 'He who hears my word does not see death for eternity' (John 8:51).

Look if it is possible to be made new against all my enemies (Ps 6:8) and to have another mind. He who lives with righteousness, always living in renewal according to the newness of the spirit and the new covenant; because, having departed from the praiseworthy life through our inattention, having become old according to the antiquity of that man, whom Paul advises to strip off (for his life is vain), that we may put on the new man created according to God in holiness and knowledge of the truth (Eph 4:22-24); such is the unblemished life.

You will understand that these things are said also regarding the invisible enemies and evil powers who have prepared a device against him, who are envious of his progress according to God, and who, after sin, speak wickedly, 'There is no salvation for him in his God' (Ps 6:10).

He prays with good intention for the enemies; for he wants them to be ashamed because of what I do, since they became enemies of the righteous and of God. And this will be beneficial to them; for he who, being ashamed and troubled by the evil working through him, having recognized it...

title: The Distinction of Righteousness
english: He will cease to act in such a way. The interpretation is confirmed by the approaching verse: 'the enemies, having been turned, no longer driving forward toward evil, but turning back into the virtuous life they left behind.' This happens to them for a good purpose, not by chronological succession or slowly, but let it happen very quickly.

Psalm 7:1: 'The son of Jemini was called from the people' (Ps 7:1), who was Saul, and Shimei, who denounced the message to Saul, a son of Arahi from his father, and the high priest was the leader of the friends and an old man according to friendship. He sings the psalm practically, while also bringing it forth theoretically. It is said in the inscription of the fourth that the psalm denotes practice, while the ode denotes theory; and since there are inscriptions having 'Psalm of an Ode' or 'Ode of a Psalm,' it must be said about them that Psalm 8 is a theory concerning practical and moral instruction, while Ode is the practice necessary to be received in contemplating the truth; for many things are done for the sake of the theory of wisdom, and no one will say a 'Psalm of an Ode' without purpose. These things being observed as an ode, it is fitting that David sings the present psalm practically while contemplating theoretically concerning each of the things being done wisely and very Godward, desiring to know what is signified by those things being accomplished in such a sensory way. And the words of the psalm beginning in such a way must also be set forth: 'Lord my God, etc.'

Psalm 7:2-3: 'Who is it that said, Saving is not from me, he who has come to seek and to save the lost, and to give his soul as a ransom for many?' (Ps 7:2-3). These signify that the Father God saves through the Son, the existing Word of God; therefore, even in the present matters, the divinity of Father and Son must not be divided, as some might suppose.

Psalm 7:7-8: 'I beseech you, Lord, arising in wrath, appear high at the ends of the enemies; for the end of iniquity will consume those things through which my enemies occur.' (Ps 7:7-8). It is possible to say the ends of the enemies are their arrogance and pride, upon which they have reached and consider themselves to be secure, thinking themselves to be in the best states. The prayer is not defensive; for he does not give back evil for evil.

When God, sparing the enemies who oppose Him, wishes them to know how God is exalted in their borders, He uses wrath not against their essence, but against the malicious intention they possess. Since the Scripture says, 'In the borders of my enemies,' it is revealed that those enemies are the enemies of the Holy and God. Psalm 7:9: 'Bring Your judgment upon me only according to Your wickedness and my righteousness; for I shall be justified when no iniquity is found in my deeds.' Regarding 'wickedness' here, he says, one must not lack goodness according to what is written, 'The innocent believes all words,' but rather the simplicity that cleanses from deceit, as signified by what is said to God by the Holy One: 'But I have taken hold of you through innocence,' and 'In innocence I have gone forward.' In certain copies, 'Judge me, Lord, according to Your righteousness,' the word is to be explained thus: there is a righteousness of God reaching to men, being distributed toward a lower righteousness.

Paul, writing about the difference of these things concerning the Jews, says, 'For I testify to them that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge; for knowing not the righteousness of God, but seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to the righteousness of God' (Romans 10:2-3). By saying the righteousness of God, he means that which comes to all who believe through Jesus Christ, which He Himself also desired. He says all things were sent so that one might be found having the righteousness from God through faith and not his own. Wishing this to be present also for the disciples, Jesus says to them, 'If your righteousness does not exceed that of the Scribes and Pharisees, you will by no means enter the kingdom of heaven' (Matthew 5:20). This distinction between human righteousness and that of God, according to the will of the Lord, is to be judged, knowing how this judgment will lead Him to salvation.

Psalm 7:10–11: 'To God belongs the examining and searching of hearts'; this does not signify merely seeking and tracing, but having a perfect apprehension; for He is a knower of hidden things, and every mind is revealed to Him.
